Because the national election was never meant to amount to much of anything. Let me explain:

Have you ever wondered why we call these small localities "states," but the rest of the world regards a State as a country/nation? Well, our fore-fathers wanted each state to be an independently-run entity, much like an independent country. Each state would make laws regarding their own life, their own government, and their own standards... after all, life in New York is MUCH different than life in Georgia.

The idea was that, like the EU (much later in time), each state would have complete sovereignty and independence. They would decide on their own education regulations, taxation, election standards, abortion laws, marriage laws, emission regulations, etc. Hell, each state has their own Constitution, Congress, and Supreme Court. They're designed to run like small, independent countries... but be United as States.

In order to be "united," there would have to be a FEW concessions... like a standard currency (the US dollar), no passport when crossing state borders, standardized road signage and systems, and free trade amongst states... like the Euro and EU regulations. In order to organize these things, the federal government was established to play a minimal role in people's everyday lives.

The national government was only instated to quell differences between states. If StateA wants to trade one way, and StateB wants to trade another, the federal government is there to help work out a compromise. They're not there to determine each state's marriage laws, abortion stance, or even how to regulate their schools... that's up to the state to decide. The federal government only exists to standardize interstate commerce and interstate regulations.

On top of that, the president is designed only to be the Commander in Chief (head of the military) and a checks and balances for this minimized federal government, so that they don't get out of hand. Because of this small role, the presidential election was never meant to be a big event... which makes the Electoral College (EC) understandable... but let's understand the EC before we understand why they exist...

See, the way we use the EC now makes it broken. Again, when your state makes all the rules/regulations, the important elections become the local ones: your governor, Senator, House representative, sheriff, mayor, etc. They're the ones making your laws, appointing your police commissioner, and electing the federal government. Since they're the ones interacting directly with their people, and the people's votes, they're the ones that have the most power. And, since the federal government is so small and abstract from the people, the votes for the federal government would be small and abstract from the people... through the EC.

You vote for your local government, the local governments vote for the federal government, and that makes the local elections the most important. Again, they're the ones making the laws, and if you don't like the laws, elect someone different, or move to a new state... which doesn't seem like a big deal to people who traveled across the Atlantic on a piece of wood.

In other words, everyone votes for the body that governs them. Your local government makes laws that regulate how you work/live, so you vote for the local government; the federal government makes laws that regulate how the local government works/lives, so the local government votes for them. Since the federal government has such little impact on the citizens, the citizens shouldn't need to vote directly for their federal government... just tell their local officials how to vote when those national elections come about... just like the EC!

These people are also designed to vote for the president, since that role isn't supposed to directly impact ANYONE except for the armed forces and other members of the federal government, which isn't supposed to do much more than decide on standard interstate road signage.

But, sadly, we've broken the system and turned things around. We have let the federal government take control of our states, making the EC a broken system. Now, the president makes decisions that impact EVERYONE when his job was designed to impact NOBODY... a single man making decisions that effect millions of people. This isn't feasible, possible, or even a good idea. So, why is it like this?

All of this happened during the Civil War, when certain states wanted to free slaves, impose certain types of taxes, and other state-centric regulations... but other states wanted to handle all of these things differently. Again, life in Massachusetts and NY is HIGHLY different than life in Georgia or Florida. This should be good and well, with the way the country was designed, right?

Well, this independence wasn't good enough, and some states wanted to IMPOSE their local laws on all of the other states. This had nothing to do with trade, road systems, or currency... but the federal government decided to intervene and take away state sovereignty. They stepped in, forced laws onto states, and angered the citizens. Many "independent" states wanted to secede from the federal government which was imposing on their freedoms (the Union) and argued that it was their right.

These arguments led to debates, which led to fighting, which led to battles, which led to war... an American Civil War.

This is being repeated in Europe, with the EU: some States want to take in "refugees" (we won't go into that definition, since this post is already so long) and others don't. Each State is a sovereign, independently-run country with its own leader and government, but the EU is stomping all over their right to decide who they give citizenship to, and now States are leaving the EU... but not without opposition.

This is how the American Civil War began, and we all know how that ended: sovereignty died and the system became broken. The over-imposing federal government took away the ability of the state to regulate itself, and began stealing power. Now, instead of your local government making your laws, most laws are decided on a federal level: marriage, abortion, emissions, education, rights to work, weapons laws, drugs/medication, etc. Sure, there's some lateral movement for states, but that's going away FAST. Just 200 years ago, each state made up all of their own laws, and now each state is regulated in almost every facet.

This is why each state has independent laws on national elections, why the EC is broken, and why the EC exists at all. That remaining lateral movement still "exists," but many don't understand why. The federal government has left the menial, meaningless tasks to the local governments, because they can't be bothered to regulate if you use a paper ballot, electronic ballot, or a chad.

It ultimately doesn't matter, because you're not going to vote in the IMPORTANT elections anyway!

TL;DR: It's different because the national government was NEVER designed to have this much power, and national elections were NEVER designed to be a big deal in any capacity.
